dataSources.title: Where our numbers come from
dataSources.intro: This game uses real NASA science. Here is every real number, where it comes from, and what the game makes up.
dataSources.savedOn: Saved NASA space-weather data was downloaded on {{date}}.
dataSources.gameNumbersIntro: We chose these numbers so the game is fair and fun. Each one is a game number, not a NASA measurement.

gameNumberNames.nightAirLoss: Air lost when the machine cannot run
gameNumberNames.doseOutsideExtra: Extra space-ray meter rise for outside work
gameNumberNames.doseBurstOutside: Particle-burst dose outside (game scale; the 39× normal-day ratio is real)
gameNumberNames.dustFactor: Rounded dusty-panel multiplier (based on the real dust effect)
gameNumberNames.foodGain: Food made when the greenhouse runs
gameNumberNames.foodLoss: Food used when the greenhouse is skipped
gameNumberNames.scienceGain: Science earned by one science trip

simplifies.crew: This game has 3 crew members. A real base would have many more people and jobs.
simplifies.sols: Our short sols are game rounds. Real storm clouds take several days to reach Mars; we squeeze that into a sol or two.
simplifies.costs: Job costs (power, food, the size of each bar) are game numbers we chose so the game is fair and fun.
simplifies.dose: The space-ray meter uses game units. The size of a storm compared with a normal day is real.
simplifies.forecast: Earth's storm warning is a computer forecast, not a measurement. Our dust forecast is made up for the game.
simplifies.dates: Normal Mars radiation was measured in 2012–13; the big storm happened in 2024.
simplifies.real: Real: the 20 May 2024 storm, normal Mars radiation, the dust effect on solar panels, and the message delay.

panels.done: Clean panels make full power tomorrow.
panels.skipped: Dust builds up. Less power tomorrow.

greenhouse.skipped: 1 less food. No food makes someone too tired.

shelter.done: Fewer space rays today and tomorrow.
shelter.skipped: No cover if a space-ray storm hits.

askEarth.skipped: You plan tomorrow without a forecast.

science.done: +1 science. 2 science trips win the science star.

crew.name: Astronaut {{n}}
crew.idleWarning: An astronaut with no job is a wasted worker.

planHelp.howTo: Tap an astronaut. Then tap a job.
planHelp.notEnoughPower: Not enough power for this job.

sol.title: Sol
sol.text: A sol is one day on Mars. It is about 40 minutes longer than an Earth day.

power.title: Power
power.text: Solar panels turn sunlight into power. Jobs inside the base use some.

air.title: Air
air.text: The air machine makes air to breathe. It needs power every night.

dose.title: Space-ray meter
dose.text: Space rays come from the Sun and from deep space. Scientists call them radiation. Too much is bad for astronauts, so keep this meter low.

food.title: Food
food.text: The greenhouse grows food under lamps. With no food, an astronaut gets too tired to work.

dust.title: Dust
dust.text: Mars dust settles on solar panels. Dusty panels make less power. A dust storm cut a real lander's power by about a third.

burst.title: Space-ray storm
burst.text: Sometimes the Sun blasts out space rays. They reach Mars in under an hour. That is too fast for Earth to warn you.

stormCloud.title: Storm cloud
stormCloud.text: A storm cloud is a huge gas cloud from the Sun. It takes days to reach Mars. So Earth can see it coming and warn you.

askEarth.title: Ask Earth
askEarth.text: Your message takes about 12 minutes to reach Earth. Scientists study it overnight. Their answer is waiting for you in the morning.

teacher.title: For teachers
teacher.goal: On Mars, every choice costs something, and help from Earth can't always arrive in time.
teacher.howTo: Play one mission (about 8 minutes). Talk about the questions. Then play again.
teacher.q1: Who waited for Earth's answer? Was it worth the wait?
teacher.q2: Which skipped job hurt your base the most? How did you find out?
teacher.q3: Why can Earth warn you about a storm cloud but not about a space-ray storm?
teacher.real: The 20 May 2024 solar storm, normal Mars radiation, dust on solar panels, and the Earth–Mars message delay are real NASA science. Job costs are game numbers.

notice.sunQuiet: The Sun is quiet toward Mars this month, so you get the May 2024 mission.
notice.sunPassed: The newest storm cloud from the Sun has already passed Mars, so you get the May 2024 mission.

moreData.title: More real data
moreData.intro: Real measurements and pictures from NASA, plus ideas from the Canadian Space Agency.

storm.title: The storm, measured on Mars
storm.chartLabel: Radiation measured by the Curiosity rover on Mars, 15 to 25 May 2024. The line jumps up on 20 May 2024.
storm.body: On a normal day, Curiosity measured about {{normal}} µGy every hour. On 20 May 2024 it shot up to about {{peak}} µGy an hour. That is about {{times}} times normal! A few days later it was back to normal.
storm.unit: µGy (microgray) is a tiny unit for how much radiation something soaks up.
storm.inGame: In the game: this is why the space-ray meter jumps in a particle burst, and why the shelter matters.
storm.source: Data: {{attribution}}. Each point on the line is a one-hour average.

site.title: Where is our base?
site.body: Our pretend base is at Gale Crater on Mars. The real Curiosity rover works there.
site.alt: Map of Gale Crater on Mars seen from above: a big round crater with a mountain in the middle
site.explore: Explore Mars yourself in NASA Mars Trek

pictures.title: Real pictures
pictures.dust: NASA's InSight lander got so dusty that its solar panels made much less power.
pictures.storm: During the 20 May 2024 storm, space rays hit Curiosity's camera and made white specks.

plants.title: Real plants grown in space
plants.body: Astronauts really grew food on the International Space Station. Scientists keep what they learned in NASA's space-biology library (OSDR).
plants.count: Search OSDR for “Veggie”, the space garden, and you find {{n}} studies.

sun.title: What the Sun did this month
sun.intro: In the 30 days up to {{date}}, NASA counted:
sun.flaresMissing: NASA's solar flare list was not available when we checked, so we leave flares out.
sun.note: NASA watches the Sun from near Earth. Most of these storms never reach Mars.

apod.title: Space picture of the day
apod.open: See it on NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day

teach.body: Free activities from the Canadian Space Agency, to keep exploring after the game.

menu.tagline: Fix it now. Or pay for it later.
menu.intro: Explore the base. Make a plan. Discover what happens next.
menu.silent: Music is off at first. Slide it up if you like.
menu.sunTodayHint: Play with what the Sun is really doing now.
menu.sunMayHint: Play the big storm that really hit Mars in May 2024.

play.chooseCrew: Choose an astronaut to change their job.
play.previewMeaning: Your plan, after jobs, night needs and solar charging.
play.idleConfirm: {{count}} available crew have no job. End anyway?
play.gameUnits: Meters and job costs use game numbers.
play.nightSummary: The base rests. Your choices keep working.
play.earthInbox: A message you earned from Earth

world.name: Ares Research Station
world.objective: Walk to the glowing console to plan your mission.
world.canvas: Mars station. Use WASD or arrow keys. Press E near a console or crew member.
world.description: In the room: a mission console in the middle, engineering shelves on the left, a science lab on the right, an airlock at the bottom, and four friends to talk to: Commander Nova, Engineer Kai, Scientist Amara and the drone Pip.
world.goConsole: Skip the walk: go to the console
world.tip: Meet your crew. They have useful advice.

commander.hello: Welcome, commander! Three astronauts. Three days. One shared home.
commander.advice: Choose each job carefully. Skipped jobs can cause problems tomorrow.

engineer.hello: I keep our lights on. Mars dust is everywhere!
engineer.advice: Clean panels make more power. The air machine needs power nightly.

scientist.hello: Our plants grow food. Our trips collect science.
scientist.advice: Two science trips earn a star. Keep everyone fed, too!

drone.hello: Hello! I'm Pip. I help keep this station running.
drone.advice: Build the shelter before space rays arrive. Lower dose is better.

airlock.hello: Surface trips are assigned through the mission console.
airlock.advice: Outside jobs collect science or clean panels. Watch the space rays!

storm.name: The Storm Season
storm.hook: Can you keep 3 astronauts safe through a real solar storm?
storm.brief: A real storm from the Sun is on its way. Nobody knows the hour. Plan each sol with care.
storm.real: Every storm here is real. A NASA rover measured each one on Mars.
storm.planners: Real crews hide in a shielded corner during solar storms.

dust.name: Dust Season
dust.hook: Dust stopped a real Mars lander. Can your base keep its lights on?
dust.brief: Dust falls on the panels every sol. Less light means less power. Pick a site and keep the base warm.
dust.real: Dust cut the power of NASA's InSight lander to about one tenth.
dust.planners: The InSight team dropped sand next to a panel. The wind then carried some dust away.

moon.name: South Pole Outpost
moon.hook: Sunlight, ice or a view of Earth? You cannot have all three.
moon.brief: NASA studied 13 landing spots near the Moon's south pole. Some are sunny. Some are near ice. Choose yours.
moon.real: NASA chose those spots for sunlight, radio contact with Earth and ice.
moon.planners: Planners look for long sunlight, a view of Earth and safe ground.

siteMars.title: Where do we land?
siteMars.text: Three real places. A real NASA robot worked in each one.

gale.label: Gale Crater
gale.real: Curiosity measured −71 °C at night here. Reading from 25 August 2026.

elysium.label: Elysium Planitia
elysium.real: Dust piled up on the InSight lander here for four years.

meridiani.label: Meridiani Planum
meridiani.real: Wind sometimes blew the dust off the Opportunity rover here.

wipe.title: Dust on the panels
wipe.text: Go outside and wipe them? Every wipe is time under space rays.

upgrade.title: Build one upgrade
upgrade.text: You have spare parts for one upgrade. Building it costs power today.

shelf.label: Greenhouse shelf: more food each harvest

walls.label: Thicker shelter walls: fewer space rays

none.label: Build nothing and save the power

radio.title: Radio Earth
radio.text: The sky is full of dust. Ask Earth how long it will last?

skip.label: Stay quiet and save the power

radioMoon.title: Radio Earth
radioMoon.text: Earth is close. The answer comes back in seconds. Ask about the Sun?

skip.label: Stay quiet and save the power

cold.title: A very cold night
cold.text: Tonight will be bitter cold. The plants may freeze.

devil.title: A dust devil!
devil.text: A tall swirl of wind is passing the base. Wind can clean panels.

tilt.label: Tilt the panels into the wind

crew.title: {{crew}} needs help
crew.text: {{crew}} is worn out and very hungry.

rover.title: One last drive
rover.text: The rover can fetch rock samples. Far rocks cost more power.

siteMoon.title: Where do we build?
siteMoon.text: Three real places near the Moon's south pole. Each one lacks something.

malapert.label: Malapert Massif
malapert.real: A very tall mountain. It gets much light and can sometimes see Earth.

shackleton.label: Peak near Shackleton
shackleton.real: A high crater rim, sunny most of the year. Earth is often hidden.

haworth.label: Haworth
haworth.real: Close to dark craters that may hold ice. Earth is often hidden.

skywatch.title: Sky watch
skywatch.text: A huge eruption on the Sun! It points away from the Moon. Shelter anyway?

ice.title: Drive for ice
ice.text: Ice hides in craters that never see the Sun. Ice becomes water and air.

rim.label: Scoop ice at the crater rim

deep.label: Drive deep into the dark crater

lastDay.title: The last day
lastDay.text: There is time for one more job before you leave.

charge.label: Charge the batteries for the next crew
